title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure carried out with synthetic video. A well known figure from the financial sector appeared in an AI generated video endorsing an investment opportunity and claiming significant returns. The video sat at the front of the fraud, at the point where a target decides whether to trust a stranger with money.

The AI component did one job, which was to supply a credible face at first contact. The payments, the account openings and the remote access that followed were handled by people. Catching it at that first step would have required confirming that the person shown had actually made the endorsement, and checking that the provider was authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, which is the check the police pointed to.

It is not established that the person depicted had any involvement in the scheme, and the police did not name them. No arrest, charge or finding against any party is reported.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in Ards and north Down lost £250,000 in an AI generated investment scam, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said. The victim saw an AI video featuring a well known financial sector personality. It promoted an investment opportunity and claimed significant returns. After a small initial investment, scammers contacted the victim on WhatsApp and encouraged more payments. They persuaded the victim to create multiple online accounts and gained remote access to their computer, claiming to help with the investment. Police called it sophisticated and substantial.

Fraudsters encouraged the victim to borrow money and moved funds to accounts they controlled. Police did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts. Police said a celebrity seeming to back an investment should not be treated as proof it is genuine. Superintendent Joanne Gibson of the Scamwise Partnership urged people to take time to verify financial activity and for families to talk about fraud. Police advised independently verifying who people are dealing with and checking that financial services providers are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority.
